recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if CBCC changes the current Consent provision inference semantics or explicitly wants additional explanatory narrative outside the scope of FHIR-13806.
issue_request: FHIR-13806 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core Consent. It said consent-example-notOrg is intended to be an OPT-IN consent excluding a named organization and, in the STU3 model, the provision needed type=deny.
initial_application: Commit ce4c96b9c327283d3166a799545e6483ef0d480c explicitly said it corrected CR #13806 and added the deny provision to source/consent/consent-example-notOrg.xml. Later Consent example and model refactors retained the scenario while adapting it to newer element names and semantics.
additional_context: Consent is active in source/fhir.ini and consent-example-notOrg is listed in the current Consent example collection. Later Published Consent decisions, especially FHIR-39597, moved .provision.type to Consent.decision and made provisions/subprovisions inferred reverse decisions of the previous level, so reintroducing the removed STU3 provision.type element would be incorrect.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source sets Consent.decision to permit and has a provision scoped to Organization/f001 with access/correct actions and a no-read/no-write comment; Organization/f001 is Burgers University Medical Center. Under the current StructureDefinition and FHIR-39597 semantics, that provision is the intended denial exception to the opt-in permit base decision.
